Paragraph pagination

Careful pagination keeps a paragraph readable across the page boundary. Each line belongs to the same passage, and the renderer moves a group of lines before painting when the widow and orphan constraints require it. The first page should end with a stable block of text rather than a single stranded line. On the following page the paragraph continues naturally, preserving its measure, leading, and inline emphasis. This final sentence confirms that content after the page break remains in order and is never clipped.

Following content starts after the paragraph.
